note: Tempdoc 595 §4.2 — the ONE system-health verdict derivation. The readiness→verdict predicate (`retrieval === …` / `retrieval !== …`) lives ONLY in the verdict seam (computeVerdict in verdict.ts); the Health header/footer and the status-bar tier/label CONSUME the derived verdict, they do not recompute it. A second shell-v0 site forming a verdict from `readiness.retrieval` is the §1.1 split (a 'Service degraded' header beside a '✓ All systems operational' footer) re-introduced. The search-window degradation banner (`readinessNotice`/`SearchSurface`) now CONSUMES the verdict too, so it is no longer allow-listed — the seam `verdict.ts` is the ONLY site that reads the predicate.
predicatePatternNote: Tempdoc 849 slice-3 review MEDIUM-4. The pattern requires the comparison's right-hand side to be a STRING LITERAL, because that is what forming a verdict actually looks like: `retrieval` is compared against a readiness STATE ('degraded' / 'unknown' / …). The previous bare `retrieval\s*[=!]==` matched any property named `retrieval` compared to anything, and flagged `evidenceProjection.ts` for `header.retrieval !== null` — an emptiness check on an unrelated field, which is not a verdict and which no amount of restructuring the product code should have been needed to appease. Scoping to `readiness\.` was considered and REJECTED: the seam itself destructures (`r.retrieval === 'degraded'`, verdict.ts:318-324), so a receiver-name pattern would fail the seam-integrity leg and would also miss any second site that aliased the same way. The state-literal form keeps both legs biting — verified by probe: a crafted `readiness.retrieval === 'DEGRADED'` in a non-allow-listed shell-v0 file still fails the gate.
